full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are that, the disputed house was originally alloted by the Government to one Md. Abbas Ali under Memo dated 28-8-62 followed by a proper deed of conveyance dated 10-12-62 leasing out of the land for a period of 99 years and transferred to him by hire purchase the house built thereon. On payment of the cost of the house Md Abbas Ali paid the entire cost of construction and other taxes to the Government and the possession of the disputed property was handed over to him on 19-12-62. While in peaceful possession of the aforesaid building the said Md Abbas Ali entered into an agreement for sale with the petitioner on 11-6-81 at a consideration of Taka 40,000.00. The petitioner paid a sum of Taka 35,000.00 as advance and got delivery of constructive possession as he was already there as a monthly tenant. The petitioner before entering into the agreement for sale enquired about the possible enlistment of the said property as abandoned and found the said property not to have been enlisted as such. Thereafter when the aforesaid Md Abbas Ali failed to execute and register the conveyance deed in terms of the said agreement for sale, the petitioner filed Title Suit No. 1481 of 1981 for specific performance of contract against Md Abbas Ali and the Government of Bangladesh. Neither Md Abbas Ali nor the Government contested the suit and, as such, the same was decreed ex parte by judgment and decree dated 24-8-83 by the learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Thereafter the petitioner in execution of the decree got a sale deed executed and registered through Court and ever since he has been in possession with the members of his family. It is stated that on 24-5-93 an official from the respondents visited the building and asked about the basis of the petitioner's possession and title which alarmed the petitioner and on query from the office he found the holding to have been enlisted in the Kha list subsequently published in the official Gazette. 26-12-88 purportedly under section 5(1)(b) of Ordinance 54 of 1985. It is submitted that no notice for surrendering or taking possession of the holding in question was ever issued to the petitioner. It is further submitted that section 4 of Ordinance 54 of 1985 is a prohibitory provision which ordains that no notice would be served after certain date and that the impugned enlistment was done in contravention of the said prohibitory provision. 

 3. Mr. MI Farooqui, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in view of the provision of section 5 read with section 4 of Ordinance 54 of 1985 the inclusion of the petitioner's building in the list published in the official Gazette without any notice to the petitioner as required under the said provision has rendered the listing illegal and without lawful authority. He further submits that in view of the decree of specific performance of contract in which the Government was a party in whose presence the decree was passed, the listing of the property as abandoned in the official Gazette is without lawful authority. 

 9. In this writ petition the petitioner has challenged the impugned enlistment inclusion in the official Gazette of the building also on the basis of the decree obtained in a suit for specific performance of contract. 

 10. Proviso to section 5 of the Ordinance does not contemplate a decree of specific performance of contract, rather contemplates the exemption of the property in respect of which a decree has been obtained declaring the same not to be an abandoned property. But in the instant case the petitioner's decree not being one declaring the property as not abandoned property it does not come within the proviso of section 5 as has been held in the case of CQMH Md Ayub Ali vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71.
